rationale: The correct error text lives in the page footer with no aria-describedby and no adjacency to the field, so it is not bound to the failing control.
citation: "the item that is in error is identified ..." — WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1; ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" (the message should be programmatically connected to the relevant form field using the aria-describedby attribute)

rationale: The ZIP error message is programmatically bound (via aria-describedby) to the valid Email field, not to the failing ZIP field, so the binding identifies the wrong control.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — the error message must be programmatically connected to the relevant form field using aria-describedby

rationale: aria-describedby references 'email-error' but the message element id is 'email-err', so the programmatic binding is broken and assistive technology receives no associated error.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — the message must be programmatically connected via aria-describedby (a dangling idref breaks the connection)

rationale: The Phone error is rendered directly beneath the valid Email field with no programmatic association to Phone, so the visual binding points at the wrong field.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — the message must be connected to the relevant form field (here it is adjacent to the wrong one)

rationale: The aria-describedby target stays empty while the real error is shown in a detached toast, so the field's binding resolves to no error text.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — the error message must be programmatically connected via aria-describedby (an empty target conveys nothing)

rationale: The empty Email field is the one in error, but the error text and aria-invalid are applied to the valid Username field, so the error is bound to the wrong control.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — aria-invalid and the bound message must mark the field actually in error

rationale: On submit the describedby target is removed and the message is appended to an unassociated node, leaving aria-describedby referencing a node that no longer exists.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — the message must remain programmatically connected via aria-describedby

rationale: Both First name and Last name share one describedby container, so the Last-name error is simultaneously bound to a passing field and does not unambiguously identify the failing control.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — the message must be connected to the relevant (single) form field in error

rationale: The error is placed only in a title tooltip on a warning glyph, not bound to the field via aria-describedby nor present as adjacent text, so it is not bound to the failing control.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — the message must be programmatically connected via aria-describedby

rationale: Both errors are concatenated into the Email field's describedby node; the failing Password field has no binding, so its error is stranded on a different control.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — each error message must be connected to the field that is in error

rationale: The error is injected into the node referenced by the failing field's aria-describedby and aria-invalid is set, so it is correctly bound.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — error message programmatically connected to the relevant form field using aria-describedby

rationale: The error sits immediately beneath the only field inside its wrapper, so adjacency binds it unambiguously to the failing control.
citation: "the item that is in error is identified ..." — WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1 (adjacent in-context text identifies the field)

rationale: Both failing fields receive their own error bound to their own aria-describedby target, so each error is bound to its correct control.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — each error message connected via aria-describedby to its field

rationale: On error the script creates the message with an id, sets the field's aria-describedby to it, and inserts it adjacent, so the binding is correct at the moment the error appears.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — error message programmatically connected via aria-describedby

rationale: The field's aria-describedby lists a hint id and an error id; the error token belongs to this field and receives the message, so the error remains correctly bound.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — error message connected via aria-describedby (multiple idrefs are permitted)

rationale: The error text is inside the field's own wrapping label, so it is associated with the failing control by label association.
citation: "the item that is in error is identified ..." — WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1; G83 "Providing text descriptions to identify required fields that were not completed"

rationale: The group error is bound to the fieldset via aria-describedby, so the error for the radio group is correctly associated with the control in error.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — error message connected to the relevant control via aria-describedby

rationale: Despite a convenience summary at the top, the authoritative error is still bound to the Email field via aria-describedby, so the field-level binding is correct.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — error message connected via aria-describedby to the field in error

rationale: The error is associated via aria-errormessage (conveyed when aria-invalid is true); a runner that only inspects aria-describedby/adjacency cannot deterministically confirm this binding mechanism and should abstain rather than declare the error stranded.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — aria-errormessage is an alternative association mechanism whose support the runner may not deterministically resolve

rationale: The error is both bound via aria-describedby and rendered immediately after the field, so it is unambiguously bound to the failing control.
citation: ARIA21 "Using aria-invalid to Indicate An Error Field" — error message programmatically connected via aria-describedby
